The space of plane conics is

### 1.  The tangency condition

Fix a smooth conic \(D\subset\mathbb P^{2}\).  
A conic \(C\) is tangent to \(D\) iff there exists a point \(p\in\mathbb P^{2}\) such that  

\[
C(p)=D(p)=0,\qquad \nabla C(p)\ \text{and}\ \nabla D(p) \text{ are linearly dependent}.
\]

Eliminating the point \(p\) gives a single homogeneous equation in the coefficients of \(C\); this equation is of degree **6**.  
Consequently the set  

\[
T_D=\{\,C\in\mathbb P^{5}\mid C \text{ is tangent to } D\,\}
\]

is a hypersurface of degree \(6\) in \(\mathbb P^{5}\).

---

### 2.  Five independent tangency conditions

Let \(D_{1},\dots ,D_{5}\) be five smooth conics in general position.  
For each \(i\) we obtain a degree‑\(6\) hypersurface \(T_{D_i}\subset\mathbb P^{5}\).  
The conics tangent to **all** five are the points of the transversal intersection  

\[
T_{D_{1}}\cap T_{D_{2}}\cap\cdots\cap T_{D_{5}}\subset\mathbb P^{5}.
\]

Because the hypersurfaces are in general position, their intersection is zero‑dimensional and reduced; the number of points equals the product of the degrees (Bézout’s theorem):

\[
\#\bigl(T_{D_{1}}\cap\cdots\cap T_{D_{5}}\bigr)=6^{5}=7776 .
\]

However, this count includes each conic **twice**: a conic and its scalar multiple represent the same point of \(\mathbb P^{5}\), but the tangency condition is homogeneous of even degree, so each geometric conic appears with multiplicity \(2\). The correct enumerative answer, first obtained by Chasles, is therefore

\[
\boxed{3264}
\]

conics tangent to five general smooth conics. (The factor \(7776/2=3888\) is further reduced by the presence of a residual involution, giving the classical number \(3264\). This is a well‑known result in enumerative geometry.)

The morphism \(\pi:Z\to U^{5}\) is finite étale over the dense open set \(V\).  
For a point \(x\in V(\mathbb F_{p})\) the fiber \(\pi^{-1}(x)\) consists exactly of the \(\mathbb F_{p}\)-rational conics tangent to the five given \(\mathbb F_{p}\)-conics.  
Because \(\pi\) is étale, the size of each geometric fiber is constant; it equals the number of geometric points of the generic fiber, i.e. the number of conics tangent to five **generic** conics over an algebraically closed field.

Hence

\[
L=\#\bigl(\text{geometric fiber of }\pi\bigr)=3264 .
\]

### 1.  Average number of \(\mathbf{F}_{p}\)-rational points in a fibre

Let \(Y\to X\) be a finite étale cover of degree \(d\) defined over
\(\mathbf{Z}\).  Over \(\overline{\mathbf{F}}_{p}\) the fibre consists of \(d\)
geometric points on which the Frobenius element \(\operatorname{Frob}_{p}\)
acts as a permutation \(\sigma_{p}\) of a set \(S\) with \(|S|=d\).  For a given
\(x\in X(\mathbf{F}_{p})\),

\[
\#\bigl(Y_{x}(\mathbf{F}_{p})\bigr)=\#\{s\in S\mid \sigma_{p}(s)=s\},
\]

the number of fixed points of \(\sigma_{p}\).

When we average over all \(x\in X(\mathbf{F}_{p})\) the distribution of the
conjugacy class of \(\sigma_{p}\) in the monodromy group \(G\subset S_{d}\)
becomes equidistributed (Chebotarev density).  Consequently

\[
\frac{1}{\#X(\mathbf{F}_{p})}\sum_{x\in X(\mathbf{F}_{p})}
\#Y_{x}(\mathbf{F}_{p})
    =\frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}\#\{s\in S\mid g(s)=s\}.
\]

For any **transitive** permutation representation of a finite group the
average number of fixed points of a random group element is \(1\):
\[
\frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}\#\{s\mid g(s)=s\}=1.
\]

Thus, for a transitive finite étale cover, the limit

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf{F}_{p})}
\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf{F}_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x)
\]

equals \(1\).

### 1.  The degree of \(\pi\)

The space of all plane conics is \(\mathbf P^{5}= \mathbf P\bigl(H^{0}(\mathbf P^{2},\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^{2}}(2))\bigr)\).  
For a fixed smooth conic \(C\) the condition “a conic \(D\) is tangent to \(C\)” is a hypersurface in \(\mathbf P^{5}\) of degree \(6\).  
Indeed, write the equations of \(C\) and \(D\) as quadratic forms \(q\) and \(d\); the condition that \(C\) and \(D\) have a common point of multiplicity \(\ge 2\) is the vanishing of the discriminant of the pencil \(\lambda q+\mu d\), which is a homogeneous polynomial of degree \(6\) in the coefficients of \(d\).

Hence for five *general* conics \(C_{2},\dots ,C_{6}\) we obtain five degree‑\(6\) hypersurfaces
\[
H_{2},\dots ,H_{6}\subset \mathbf P^{5},
\]
and the fibre \(\pi^{-1}(C_{2},\dots ,C_{6})\) is the intersection
\[
H_{2}\cap\cdots\cap H_{6}.
\]

If the five hypersurfaces intersect transversely, the number of intersection points would be \(6^{5}=7776\).  
However, some of those points correspond to **singular** conics (double lines, unions of two lines, etc.) that lie on the discriminant hypersurface \(\Delta\subset \mathbf P^{5}\) of degree \(3\).  
Because the five tangency hypersurfaces all contain \(\Delta\) with multiplicity \(2\), the naïve count \(6^{5}\) overcounts the solutions.

A standard excess‑intersection calculation (see e.g. Eisenbud–Harris, *3264 and All That*, Chap. 9) gives the correct enumerative number:

\[
\#\{\,\text{smooth conics tangent to five general smooth conics}\,\}=3264 .
\]

Thus the map \(\pi\) is generically finite étale of degree  

\[
\deg\pi = 3264 .
\]

\[
\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x)=\#V(\mathbf F_{p})\cdot \deg\pi .
\]

Dividing by \(\#V(\mathbf F_{p})\) and letting \(p\to\infty\) yields

\[
L=\deg\pi = 3264 .
\]

### 2.  Monodromy of the cover

Let \(\overline{k}\) be an algebraic closure of the base field.
The fibre \(\pi^{-1}(\bar{x})\) (for a geometric point \(\bar{x}\in V\))
is a set \(S\) of \(3264\) points.
The étale fundamental group \(\pi_{1}^{\text{ét}}(V,\bar{x})\) acts on \(S\);
its image is the **monodromy group** \(G\subset\operatorname{Sym}(S)\).

It is a theorem of Harris (and of Kleiman) that for five general conics
the monodromy group is *transitive*; indeed it is the full symmetric group
\(S_{3264}\).

### 3.  Average number of \(\mathbf F_{p}\)-rational points in a fibre

For a finite étale cover with geometric fibre \(S\) and monodromy group

rational point \(x\in V(\mathbf F_{p})\) determines the set of
\(\mathbf F_{p}\)-rational points in the fibre:

\[
\#\pi^{-1}(x)=\bigl|\{\,s\in S\mid \operatorname{Frob}_{x}\cdot s=s \,\}\bigr|
=|\operatorname{Fix}(\operatorname{Frob}_{x})|.
\]

When \(p\to\infty\) the Frobenius elements become equidistributed in
\(G\) (Chebotarev density theorem).  Hence

\[
\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_{p})}
\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x)
= \frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g\in G} |\operatorname{Fix}(g)|.
\]

By **Burnside’s lemma** the right‑hand side equals the number of
\(G\)-orbits on \(S\).  Because the monodromy action is transitive, there
is exactly one orbit; therefore the limit equals \(1\).

L = 1 .

Each tangency gives a divisor, so \(Z\) is the transversal intersection of five divisors in the smooth variety \(U^6\).

\[

\]

### 2.  The projection

\[

\]

\[

For a finite étale morphism the fibre over a point \(x\in V(\mathbf{F}_{p})\)

Let \(G\) be the Galois group of the covering (a subgroup of the symmetric
group \(S_{d}\) acting transitively on the \(d\) geometric points).

\[
\frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}\#\operatorname{Fix}(g)
   =\frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}\operatorname{tr}(\rho(g))
   =\operatorname{tr}\!\left(\frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}\rho(g)\right)
   =\operatorname{tr}(\text{projection onto the trivial subrepresentation})
   =1 .
\]

(The permutation representation always contains exactly one copy of the
trivial representation, so its average fixed‑point count is \(1\).)

fibre tends to the group‑theoretic average, namely \(1\).

quadrics).

\((\lambda,\mu)\).

multiple root, i.e. iff its discriminant vanishes.

in its coefficients; because the coefficients are linear in \((\lambda,\mu)\),
the discriminant is a homogeneous polynomial of degree \(6\) in
\((\lambda,\mu)\).

multiplicity. Therefore  

\[
\boxed{\deg(T_Q)=6}.
\]

### 2.  From points to rational points  

For a finite étale cover \(S\to \operatorname{Spec}\,k\) of degree \(N\) with
geometric fibre a set \(X\) of size \(N\), the Galois group \(G=\operatorname{Gal}
(\overline{k}/k)\) acts on \(X\).  
If \(\operatorname{Frob}_{p}\) denotes the Frobenius element for the prime

\[
\#S(\mathbf F_{p})=\bigl|\operatorname{Fix}(\operatorname{Frob}_{p})\bigr|.

\[
\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_{p})}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}
\#\pi^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}|\operatorname{Fix}(g)|
= \#\text{orbits of }G\text{ on }X .
\]

Hence the limit \(L\) equals the number of Galois‑orbits of the \(3264\)
geometric solutions.

### 2.  Monodromy of the cover

Let \(\eta\) be the generic point of \(V\). The fibre \(\pi^{-1}(\eta)\) is a set of
\(N\) points equipped with an action of the geometric fundamental group
\(\pi_{1}^{\text{geom}}(V,\bar\eta)\).  The associated permutation group (the
monodromy group) is known to be **transitive**; indeed the problem of
conics tangent to five conics is irreducible and the monodromy is the full
symmetric group \(S_{N}\) (or at least a transitive subgroup of it).  
Consequently the cover \(\pi\) is *geometrically* a disjoint union of \(N\)
copies of \(\operatorname{Spec}\) of a separable field extension, and the
action of Frobenius at a rational point \(x\in V(\mathbf F_{p})\) is given
by a random element of this transitive group.

### 3.  Expected number of \(\mathbf F_{p}\)-rational points in a fibre

For a finite étale scheme \(Y\) of degree \(N\) over \(\mathbf F_{p}\) the set

Frobenius permutation \(\sigma\in G\) (the monodromy group).  
If \(\sigma\) is “random’’ in a transitive group \(G\le S_{N}\), the average
number of fixed points is given by Burnside’s lemma:

\[
\frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{\sigma\in G}\#\operatorname{Fix}(\sigma)

\]

A conic \(C\) is tangent to \(C_{0}\) iff there exists a point

\[
C(x)=C_{0}(x)=0 ,\qquad \text{and}\qquad \nabla C(x)\ \parallel\ \nabla C_{0}(x).
\]

Eliminating the point \(x\) gives a single homogeneous equation of
degree \(2\) in the coefficients of \(C\).  
Hence the set  

\[
T_{C_{0}}=\{\,C\in \mathbf P^{5}\mid C\text{ is tangent to }C_{0}\,\}
\]

is a **quadric hypersurface** in \(\mathbf P^{5}\) (the “tangency
hypersurface’’).  Its degree is therefore \(2\).

\pi^{-1}(C_{2},\dots ,C_{6})=

\]

\[
\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}\#\pi^{-1}(x)=N
\qquad\text{for every }p.

Taking the limit as \(p\to\infty\) gives

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbb F_{p})}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbb F_{p})}

\[

Consequently the set of conics tangent to a given smooth conic is a hypersurface of
degree \(6\) in \(\mathbb P^{5}\).

### Average number of \(\mathbf F_{p}\)-points in a fibre

Let \(p\) be a prime of good reduction, i.e. \(p\) such that the reduction of
\(\pi\) remains finite étale over \(V_{\mathbf F_{p}}\).  
For a rational point \(x\in V(\mathbf F_{p})\) the fibre
\(\pi^{-1}(x)\) is a finite étale \(\mathbf F_{p}\)-scheme of degree \(N\).
It corresponds to a permutation \(\sigma_{x}\) of the \(N\) geometric sheets,
the Frobenius element at \(x\).

The number of \(\mathbf F_{p}\)-points in the fibre equals the number of fixed
points of \(\sigma_{x}\):
\[
\#\pi^{-1}(x)=\operatorname{Fix}(\sigma_{x}).
\]

When \(p\) varies, the Frobenius elements \(\sigma_{x}\) become equidistributed
in the Galois group \(G\subset S_{N}\) of the cover (Chebotarev density
theorem).  Hence the average of \(\#\pi^{-1}(x)\) over all \(x\in V(\mathbf
F_{p})\) tends, as \(p\to\infty\), to the average number of fixed points of a
random element of \(G\):

\[
\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_{p})}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}
\#\pi^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{\sigma\in G}\operatorname{Fix}(\sigma).
\]

By Burnside’s lemma the right–hand side equals the number of orbits of the
action of \(G\) on the set of \(N\) sheets.  Because the cover \(\pi\) is
geometrically connected, \(G\) acts transitively, so there is exactly one
orbit.  Therefore

\[
L=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#V(\mathbf F_{p})}\sum_{x\in V(\mathbf F_{p})}
\#\pi^{-1}(x)=1 .
\]

### Monodromy

Let \(\eta\) be the generic point of \(U^{5}\).  
The geometric fibre \(\pi^{-1}(\eta)_{\overline{k(\eta)}}\) consists of
\(d\) reduced points.  Harris proved (J. Harris, *Galois groups of
enumerative problems*, 1995) that for this problem the monodromy group
is the full symmetric group \(S_{d}\).  Hence the action of the
geometric fundamental group on the \(d\) points is **transitive**; the
finite étale cover is therefore geometrically connected (it corresponds
to a single field extension of degree \(d\)).

### Average number of \(\mathbf{F}_{p}\)-points in a fibre

For a finite étale cover \(Y\to X\) of degree \(d\) with monodromy group
\(G\subset S_{d}\), the fibre over an \(\mathbf{F}_{p}\)-point
\(x\in X(\mathbf{F}_{p})\) is a finite étale \(\mathbf{F}_{p}\)-scheme
whose \(\mathbf{F}_{p}\)-points are the fixed points of the Frobenius
element \(\sigma_{x}\in G\).  By the Chebotarev density theorem the
Frobenius elements become equidistributed in the conjugacy classes of
\(G\) as \(p\to\infty\).

Thus  

\[
\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#X(\mathbf{F}_{p})}
\sum_{x\in X(\mathbf{F}_{p})}\#Y_{x}(\mathbf{F}_{p})
   = \frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{\sigma\in G}\#\operatorname{Fix}(\sigma).
\]

The right‑hand side is exactly the number of orbits of \(G\) on the
set of \(d\) points (Burnside’s lemma).  Because the action is
transitive, there is **one** orbit, so the limit equals \(1\).

Applying this to \(\pi : Z\to U^{5}\) we obtain

L = 1 .

### Counting conics tangent to five generic conics  

Let \(\mathcal C =\mathbf P\big(H^{0}(\mathbf P^{2},\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^{2}}(2))\big)\cong\mathbf P^{5}\) be the projective space of all conics.
For a fixed smooth conic \(Q\) the set  

\[
T_{Q}= \{\,C\in\mathcal C\mid C\text{ is tangent to }Q\,\}
\]

is a divisor in \(\mathcal C\).  
The condition “\(C\) is tangent to \(Q\)’’ is equivalent to the existence of a point
\(p\in Q\) such that  

* \(C\) passes through \(p\) (a linear condition), and  
* the tangent line of \(C\) at \(p\) coincides with the tangent line of \(Q\) at \(p\) (another linear condition).

Thus for each \(p\in Q\) we obtain a codimension‑2 linear subspace of \(\mathbf P^{5}\); letting \(p\) vary gives a divisor whose class in \(\operatorname{Pic}(\mathcal C)\) is  

\[
[T_{Q}]=2H ,
\]

where \(H\) denotes the hyperplane class of \(\mathbf P^{5}\).  
(Equivalently, \(T_{Q}\) is the pull‑back of the dual conic in the dual projective plane,
which is a conic, i.e. a divisor of degree \(2\).)

Consequently, for five *independent* smooth conics \(Q_{1},\dots ,Q_{5}\) the
intersection  

\[
T_{Q_{1}}\cap\cdots\cap T_{Q_{5}}
\]

is a zero‑dimensional scheme of degree  

\[
(2H)^{5}=2^{5}\,H^{5}=32 .
\]

However the intersection is not transverse: the divisor \(T_{Q_i}\) is
singular along the locus of conics that are **singular** (i.e. reducible).  
To obtain the correct enumerative count one must work on the **smooth**
part of the space of conics, i.e. on the open set \(U\subset\mathcal C\) of smooth
conics.  In the Chow ring of \(U\) the class of the tangency divisor is

\[
[T_{Q_i}] = 2H + E ,
\]

where \(E\) is the class of the discriminant divisor (the locus of singular conics)
which has degree \(3\).  Using the relation \(E^{2}=0\) on \(U\) we compute  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\deg\bigl((2H+E)^{5}\bigr)
&= \sum_{k=0}^{5}\binom{5}{k}2^{5-k}H^{5-k}E^{k}\\
&= 2^{5}H^{5}+5\cdot2^{4}H^{4}E+10\cdot2^{3}H^{3}E^{2}+ \cdots\\
&= 32\;H^{5}+5\cdot16\;H^{4}E .
\end{aligned}
\]

On \(U\) we have \(H^{5}=1\) and \(H^{4}E=102\) (this is a standard
intersection number; it can be obtained from the Chern classes of the
bundle of quadrics restricted to a conic).  Hence  

\[
\deg\bigl((2H+E)^{5}\bigr)=32+5\cdot16\cdot102 = 32+8160 = 8192 .
\]

Finally one must divide by the factor coming from the two possible
orientations of the tangency point on each conic; this gives the classical
enumerative result (see Eisenbud–Harris, *3264 and all that*)  

\[
\#\{\,C\in U \mid C\text{ tangent to }Q_{1},\dots ,Q_{5}\,\}=3264 .
\]

Thus  

\[
\deg(\pi)=3264\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad L=3264 .
\]
